title: Northwind Logistics FY2024 Annual Report
text: Northwind Logistics reported revenue of 412 million dollars in fiscal 2024, up 12 percent from 368 million dollars in fiscal 2023. Operating margin held steady at 9 percent. At the close of fiscal 2024 the company operated 47 distribution centres across North America, concentrated in the Midwest and the Pacific Northwest. Headcount rose to 6,200 from 5,800 the prior year. Management attributed the revenue increase primarily to cold-chain contracts signed in the second half of the year, and noted that fuel costs remained the largest single input expense.

title: Northwind Logistics Q1 FY2025 Results
text: In the first quarter of fiscal 2025 Northwind Logistics reported revenue of 118 million dollars. The company opened three new distribution centres during the quarter, bringing the network total to 50. Management reaffirmed full-year guidance and said the cold-chain segment continued to outgrow the rest of the business. Quarterly operating margin was 8 percent, down one point year over year, which the company attributed to start-up costs at the new sites.

title: Helion Grid Company Overview
text: Helion Grid designs and operates grid-scale battery storage systems. The company was founded in 2019 and is headquartered in Mesa County. Its flagship installation, the Mesa site, has a rated capacity of 240 megawatt-hours as of the 2025 reporting year. Helion Grid sells capacity primarily through long-term offtake agreements with industrial and logistics customers rather than on the spot market. The company reported 180 employees in 2025.

title: Helion Grid 2026 Capacity Update
text: As of the 2026 update, the Mesa site capacity was expanded to 310 megawatt-hours following the commissioning of a third battery block. Helion Grid said the expansion was fully subscribed by existing offtake customers before it came online. No additional sites entered construction during the period.

title: Helion Grid 2025 Safety Review
text: Helion Grid's 2025 safety review found no thermal runaway incidents at the Mesa site during the reporting period. The review documented two minor coolant leaks, both contained without service interruption. Inspectors noted that the site's fire suppression system was tested quarterly, exceeding the minimum required frequency. The review did not assess sites outside Mesa County.

title: Varro Capital: Regional Storage Market Outlook
text: Analysts at Varro Capital estimate the regional grid storage market will reach 3.1 billion dollars by 2030. The estimate assumes permitting timelines shorten modestly and that industrial offtake demand continues at its current pace. Varro describes its own figure as the most optimistic of the published forecasts.

title: Teller Research: Regional Storage Market Forecast
text: Teller Research projects the regional grid storage market at 1.8 billion dollars by 2030, citing slower permitting and interconnection queues as the binding constraints. Teller explicitly declines to endorse the higher estimates published by other firms, including Varro Capital, and argues that those models understate grid interconnection delay.

title: Northwind Logistics and Helion Grid Supply Agreement
text: Northwind Logistics signed a ten-year supply agreement with Helion Grid in March 2025 to supply power to its distribution centres. The agreement covers the company's Midwest network initially, with an option to extend to Pacific Northwest sites. Neither party disclosed the contract value. The agreement was described as the largest single offtake commitment Helion Grid had signed to that date.

title: Mesa County Battery Storage Permitting Rule
text: Under the Mesa County permitting rule adopted in 2024, battery storage sites with a rated capacity above 200 megawatt-hours require an annual safety review filed with the county. Sites at or below that threshold file every three years instead. The rule also requires operators to notify the county within 30 days of any capacity expansion.

title: Northwind Aviation FY2024 Summary
text: Northwind Aviation, a charter operator unrelated to Northwind Logistics, reported revenue of 91 million dollars in 2024. The company operates a fleet of 18 aircraft from three regional hubs. Northwind Aviation has no corporate relationship with Northwind Logistics despite the shared name, a point it clarifies in its investor materials.
